papers.title: When Positivity Matters: Maximal Distance Integrals on Curves and Surfaces
papers.abstract: How far apart, on average, can $n$ points in a set $A$ be? As $n\to\infty$ the answer is the $\textit{maximal energy}$ $M^{+}(A)$, the largest possible value of $\mathbb{E}|X-Y|$ when $X$ and $Y$ are independent random points of $A$ with a common distribution. If the distribution is allowed to carry negative mass, we obtain a second constant $M(A)\ge M^{+}(A)$. It is often far easier to compute: when a signed equilibrium measure exists, it is characterized by a $\textit{linear}$ potential equation, whereas the positive problem must also locate the support of the mass. This paper asks when positivity matters, that is, when $M^{+}(A)<M(A)$. For polygons and polyhedra the extremal mass sits on the vertices and closed forms abound. Even so, every hollow convex polygon has $M^{+}<M$, and a simple kite shows how a vertex can be forced out of the support. For smooth curves and surfaces the answer depends on the shape. Circles and spheres have $M^{+}=M$. The ellipse $x^2+4y^2=4$ has $M^{+}=M$ numerically, and we give its value to 50 digits. The ellipses $x^2+9y^2=9$ and $x^2+25y^2=25$ have $M^{+}<M$ numerically, with gaps in the support. For the ellipsoid $10x^2+15y^2+12z^2=15$, studied by Larcher, Schmid and Wolf, we compute 50 digits of $M$ and give strong numerical evidence that $M^{+}<M$. The extremal measure vanishes on two caps around the ends of the shortest axis. Proofs and numerical methods are collected in appendices.

papers.title: Global topology and symmetry breaking in an indefinite superlinear Dirichlet problem
papers.abstract: Motivated by the work of Fencl and L\'opez-G\'omez [13] on global bifurcation diagrams, we study the connected components of positive solutions of $-u''=\lambda u+a(x)u^p$ on $(-1,1)$ with $u(-1)=u(1)=0$, where $a$ changes sign and $p\ge2$ is an integer. For generic $\mathcal C^r$ weights, $r\ge2$, with $n$ positive intervals, simple zeros and negative endpoint values, we obtain at least $2^{n-1}$ noncompact components. Apart from the principal component, each is a curve with both ends at $\lambda=-\infty$. The proof distinguishes at least $2^n-1$ ends and yields bounds for branching and compactly supported cohomology. For even weights, an odd Morse index of at least $k$ on the principal symmetric component forces at least $k$ symmetry-breaking points. In particular, symmetry breaking occurs if $a(0)<0$.

papers.title: Kinetic transfer or regularity in any dimension from uncertainty inequalities on the real line
papers.abstract: The purpose of this short note is to show that one dimensional uncertainty inequalities easily induce transfer of regularity inequalities in kinetic equations in any dimension.

papers.title: Sharp Estimates for Jacobi Heat Kernels on a Ball and on a Simplex in the Full Range of Parameters
papers.abstract: We establish genuinely sharp heat-kernel estimates for orthogonal expansions on the Euclidean unit ball and on the unit simplex throughout their natural parameter ranges. For the ball weight $W_\mu(x)=(1-\|x\|^2)^{\mu-1/2}$, we extend the known estimate from the range $\mu\geq0$ to every $\mu>-1/2$. For the simplex, we prove the corresponding estimate for every $\kappa\in(-1/2,\infty)^{d+1}$. The estimates retain exactly the form known in the classical ranges. The proof is based on analytic continuation of the classical product and reduction formulas. Below the integrability threshold, the ball formula decomposes into an endpoint term and a derivative correction, while the simplex formula produces endpoint and mixed-derivative terms indexed by the negative coordinates. In the lowest simplex parameter range we use the auxiliary even ultraspherical kernel introduced by Nowak, Sj\"ogren, and Szarek.

papers.title: Two-Dimensional Local Smoothing in Noncommutative Spaces and Its Applications
papers.abstract: We prove local smoothing for planar half-waves with coefficients in a semifinite tracial von Neumann algebra $M$. For $N\ge2$ and $P_N=\psi(|D|/N)$ with $\psi\in C_c^\infty((1/2,2))$, we obtain $\|e^{it|D|}P_N f\|_{L^4([1,2]\times\mathbb{R}^2;L^4(M))}\le C_\psi\sqrt{\log(2+N)}\|f\|_{L^4(\mathbb{R}^2;L^4(M))}$ uniformly in $M$ and its trace. Pairing the Dirichlet energies for $M$ and its opposite algebra cancels a determinant contribution that can have either sign. At $p=4$, summation over frequency annuli gives local smoothing for every Sobolev order $s>0$. Interpolating the annular estimates before summation gives spacetime $L^p$ bounds for $2\le p\le\infty$ and Sobolev orders $s>\sigma(p)=\max\{0,1/2-2/p\}$, as well as logarithmically weighted bounds at $s=\sigma(p)$ for $2<p<\infty$. The finite-$p$ bounds transfer to quantum tori and generalized Moyal planes, answering the question of Hong, Lai and Wang about the range $s>\sigma(p)$ for $2<p<\infty$ on generalized Moyal planes. For $1<p<\infty$ and complex $\alpha$ with $\operatorname{Re}\alpha>\max\{2/p-1,1/p-1/2,-1/p\}$, we prove maximal inequalities over all radii for generalized circular means on the plane, quantum tori and generalized Moyal planes. For an action $\beta$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$ on $M$ by normal trace-preserving $*$-automorphisms with norm-continuous $L^p$ orbits, the orbit mean $A_{t,\beta}^\alpha x$ converges bilaterally almost uniformly to $\pi x/\Gamma(1+\alpha)$ as $t\downarrow0$ for every $x\in L^p(M)$. We also obtain estimates for truncated cone multipliers on three-dimensional Euclidean and quantum Euclidean spaces, and full-radius row and column bounds for Stein's square function on the plane, quantum tori and generalized Moyal planes.

papers.title: Riesz Transform Bounds Imply Parabolic Uniform Rectifiability of Graphs
papers.abstract: We prove that if a $(k+2)$-Ahlfors--David regular measure $\mu$ in parabolic space $\mathbb P^n$ has support equal to a parabolic Lipschitz graph with sufficiently small Lipschitz constant, and the parabolic Riesz transform is bounded on $L^2(\mu)$, then $\mu$ is parabolic uniformly rectifiable and the graph is regular parabolic Lipschitz. The result holds for every integer $0\leq k\leq n-1$.

papers.title: Perturbed Nevo--Thangavelu maximal functions on two-step nilpotent groups
papers.abstract: Consider a step-two nilpotent Lie group $G$ identified with $\mathbb R^d\times \mathbb R^m$ in exponential coordinates. We study maximal operators associated with parabolic dilates of smooth convex hypersurfaces with nonvanishing Gaussian curvature in a tilted $d$-dimensional subspace of $G$. We focus on the low-rank regime, where the rank is determined by the group law and the tilt. When $m=1$, we determine the optimal range of $p$ for which the maximal operator is bounded on $L^p(G)$. For $m\ge2$, we characterize, in terms of a {\L}ojasiewicz exponent, when the known necessary condition on $p$ is also sufficient.

papers.title: Vector Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals, higher derivatives of Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals and boundedness of solutions of functional-differential equations of retarded type
papers.abstract: In present paper, for functional-differential equations of retarded type, the method of vector Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals and the method of higher derivatives of Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals are developed. On the basis of this methods, sufficient conditions for various types of uniform boundedness of solutions and sufficient conditions for various types of ultimate-uniform boundedness of solutions are obtained.

papers.title: Differential equations for Macdonald's hypergeometric series via Dunkl operators of type A
papers.abstract: We solve an eigenvalue problem for a family of trigonometric Dunkl operators depending on a parameter, extending the result of Ref.[16] to the case of a general parameter. We introduce families of nonsymmetric W-type operators closely related to Dunkl operators and analyze their algebraic structure, various representations and symmetrization. We then use these operators to characterize non-symmetric Macdonald's hypergeometric series introduced in Ref.[5] and recover several known results. These results suggest a direct connection between Macdonald's hypergeometric series and Dunkl operators.

papers.title: Qualitative WALA, Alberti representations and Lipschitz differentiability
papers.abstract: We show that the existing theory of Lipschitz differentiability spaces implies that a metric measure space satisfying a qualitative analogue of the WALA condition of David--Semmes has many independent Alberti representations, and provides conditions for when such a space is rectifiable.

papers.title: A surprising bound for the $2\times2$ matrix weighted martingale multiplier
papers.abstract: For real $2\times2$ matrix weights, we prove that a scalar martingale multiplier on a dyadic root has $L^2(W)$ norm at most $CQ\sqrt{1+\log(Q)}$, where $Q$ is the dyadic matrix $A_2$ characteristic. A single multiplier, with signs alternating by generation, attains this order for every sufficiently large characteristic scale. We show that the restriction on the matrix size is essential: these estimates jump to the order $Q^{3/2}$ from the matrix size $3\times 3$ onward.

papers.title: The dimensions of curly and dipolar Besicovitch-Kakeya sets
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish sharp Hausdorff dimension and box-counting dimension bounds for sets containing meridian circles and for sets whose difference sets contain a sphere. Fix two antipodal points N, S on S^{n-1}, n\ge 3, and consider the family of great circles passing through them. Assuming the Besicovitch-Kakeya overlapping conjecture in R^{n-1}, we prove that every bounded set K\subset R^n containing a translated and dilated copy of each circle in this family satisfies \dim_H K\ge n-1. In particular, the same conclusion holds for bounded sets containing a circle in every orientation. This bound is sharp, as shown by the unit sphere. We also prove unconditionally that every bounded set K\subset R^n, n\ge2, satisfying S^{n-1}\subset K-K has lower box counting dimension greater than or equal to n(n-1)/(2n-1), and the bound is also sharp.

papers.title: On the Bourgain-Rudnick eigenfunction restriction conjecture in four dimensions
papers.abstract: We prove a uniform upper $L^2$ bound for eigenfunctions of the four-dimensional flat torus on the compact paraboloid $\mathbb{P}^3$. The main novelty is the use of Fourier restriction estimates. We interpret spherical lattice point statistics as non-concentration inequalities of the strength needed to apply the Du--Zhang fractal restriction theorem. We apply their result on two-dimensional slices of $\mathbb{P}^3$. Further possible extensions are also discussed.

papers.title: Sharp constant off-diagonal extrapolation for Muckenhoupt bases
papers.abstract: In this paper we prove a sharp constant version of off-diagonal extrapolation for matrix weights, improving the result we proved in an earlier paper. In an appendix, we give a new and simpler proof of this result in the scalar case.

papers.title: OpenAI's proof of the local smoothing conjecture: A harmonic analytic perspective
papers.abstract: This note presents OpenAI's proof of the local smoothing conjecture. It is written for harmonic analysts who may be new to quaternionic Monge--Amp\`ere equations. We introduce the quaternionic Hessian and explain how the associated determinant equation leads to the critical annular estimate.

papers.title: On the measure of Neighborhoods of Kakeya and Truncated Nikodym Sets
papers.abstract: We show that there exist Kakeya sets in $\mathbb{R}^d$ whose $\delta$-neighborhoods have measure $\lesssim |\log\delta|^{-(d-1)}$. We also show that the measure of a $\delta$-neighborhood of an $\epsilon$-truncated Nikodym set in $\mathbb{R}^2$ $\gtrsim \epsilon^{-1}|\log\delta|^{-1}$, for $\delta$ small enough. The sufficiently small scale depends on the Nikodym set and on $\epsilon$.

papers.title: The $T1$ theorem under Dini regularity
papers.abstract: We prove the $T1$ theorem for Calder\'on-Zygmund operators under the classical Dini regularity condition on the kernel, solving a longstanding open problem in singular integral theory.

papers.title: Common tiles from fractional tiles for two lattices
papers.abstract: Let $L_1, L_2\subseteq{\mathbb R}^d$ be lattices of the same volume and let $D_1, D_2$ be two bounded fundamental domains for $L_1, L_2$. We show that there is a measurable common tile for $L_1$ and $L_2$ contained in $D_1+D_2$. The main tool is a result of Bowen, Kun and Sabok (2021) which shows how to obtain a measurable perfect matching given a fractional perfect matching in hyperfinite graphings.

papers.title: Weighted Bergman projection in radial trees
papers.abstract: We study the Bergman projection $P_\omega $ on a radial tree with respect to weighted harmonic Bergman spaces $A^p_\omega $, where $\omega $ is a positive radial weight. We prove that for all such weights and $1<p<\infty $, the Bergman projection $P_\omega $ is bounded from $L^p(\omega) $ to $A^p_\omega $ and $L^\infty \to \mathcal{B} $, where $\mathcal{B} $ is the Bloch space of the tree. We also provide a characterization of the weights $\omega $ for which the positive Bergman projection $P_\omega^+ $ is bounded from $L^p(\omega) $ to $L^p(\omega) $. Finally, in the appendix, we provide an elementary proof of the characterization of the weights $\Omega \in L^1(\mathbb{D}) $ for which the Bergman projection from $L^p(\Omega) $ to the holomorphic Bergman space $A^p_\Omega(\mathbb{D}) $.

papers.title: Trigonal Elliptic Coordinates on the Sphere and Some Applications
papers.abstract: We construct a theta-function parametrization of the unit sphere adapted to the eight trigonal directions. The construction follows from a cubic theta identity discussed by Bobek and admits an equivalent representation in Jacobi elliptic functions. The angular parameter and theta nome give a nonorthogonal coordinate system whose squared Cartesian components are related to the three-component Volterra chain. An algebraic change of angle, retaining the nome, yields orthogonal coordinates with explicit metric coefficients and a diagonal Laplace--Beltrami operator. We apply both parametrizations to the geometry of O'Brien's reduced Jahn--Teller model and give compact expressions for real spherical harmonics of degrees two and three. The orthogonal angle is the polar angle of an $E_g$ quadrupolar doublet, while one octupolar harmonic depends only on the nome within each octant.

papers.title: Rational extensions of the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process
papers.abstract: We introduce and classify rational extensions of the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process that are solvable by polynomials. These diffusions are closely related to exceptional Hermite polynomials and rational extensions of the quantum harmonic oscillator. We obtain explicit formulas for their transition densities, fundamental solutions and Green functions. We also show that each such diffusion can be constructed from killed Brownian motion by a finite sequence of Darboux transformations followed by a Doob $h$-transform. Finally, we derive an explicit formula for the connection polynomials in the generalized Mehler formula and use it to prove several conjectures concerning these polynomials.

papers.title: Mahler's problem and Turyn polynomials
papers.abstract: Mahler's problem asks for the largest possible value of the Mahler measure, normalized by the $L_2$ norm, of a polynomial with $\pm1$ coefficients and large degree. We establish a new record value of approximately $0.951$ in this problem by analyzing certain Turyn polynomials, which are defined by cyclically shifting the coefficients of a Fekete polynomial by a prescribed amount. Recently, Klurman, Lamzouri, and Munsch established that the distribution of values over the unit circle of Fekete polynomials of large degree is effectively modeled by a particular random point process. We extend this analysis to the Turyn polynomials, and determine expressions for the asymptotic normalized Mahler measure of these polynomials, as well as for their normalized $L_q$ norms. We also describe a number of calculations on the corresponding random processes, which indicate that the Turyn polynomials where the shift is approximately $1/4$ of the length have Mahler measure exceeding $95\%$ of their $L_2$ norm. Further, we show that these asymptotic values are not disturbed by a small change to make polynomials having entirely $\pm1$ coefficients, which establishes the result on Mahler's problem. We also estimate that the limiting value of the normalized $L_1$ norm of these polynomials exceeds $0.977$, in connection with a question of Newman.

papers.title: Liouvillian integrability of vector fields in higher dimensions
papers.abstract: We consider complex rational vector fields in dimension $n>2$ (equivalently, differential forms of degree $n-1$ in $n$ variables) which admit a Liouvillian first integral. Extending a classical result by Singer for $n=2$, our main result states that there exists a first integral which is obtained by two successive integrations from one-forms with coefficients in a finite algebraic extension of the rational function field. The proof uses Puiseux series in a novel way to simplify computations. We also apply this method to give elementary proofs of Singer's theorem for rational one-forms, and of the Prelle-Singer theorem on elementary integrability of rational vector fields.

papers.title: Harmonic weights in inverse central binomial series
papers.abstract: We study how the partial fraction coefficients of an inverse central binomial series change when the harmonic weight $H_{pn}$ is replaced by $H_{qn}$. For positive integers $p<q$, every coefficient increases. As the index $k$ grows, the increase tends to $2\log(q/p)$ uniformly over all angles $0<\phi\le\pi$, even when the angle approaches either endpoint. The increase is above the limit at every odd index and below it at every even index. We give the first correction, of order $k^{-2/q}$ for $q>2$ and of order $k^{-2}$ for $(p,q)=(1,2)$. For the normalized transforms, subtracting $c$ times the first from the second gives a Stieltjes function exactly when $c\le1$. We also determine which real dilations $0<p<q$ satisfy the same sign law. For $p\ge1$ it holds exactly when $q\ge2$. For $0<p<1$ it holds above a threshold $Q(p)$, and at the threshold it holds precisely on one interval $0<p<p_*$. Finally, we give angle identities at every odd weight from three onward and determine which Dirichlet $L$-terms cancel at angle $\pi/3$.

papers.title: Differential inclusions and the chattering phenomenon
papers.abstract: This is a second draft of a manuscript about existence of solutions of differential inclusions involving chattering.

papers.title: Algebraic Hodge generic points are dense
papers.abstract: Let $f: X \to S$ be a quasi-projective family of varieties defined over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}} \subset \mathbb{C}$. We show that the points of $S(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ that are Hodge generic for the variation of Hodge structures associated to $f$ are analytically dense in $S(\mathbb{C})$. In fact, in the spirit of the Grothendieck period conjecture and under a large monodromy assumption, we prove the density of the points of $S(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})$ where the periods of the fibre do not satisfy extra relations 'up to degree $\delta$'. As a by-product, we also establish new instances of the Mumford-Tate conjecture, beyond the realm of abelian motives. When the base $S$ is a curve, we provide quantitative estimates for points satisfying these properties. The main technical contribution is a new result on relations satisfied by solutions of $G$-operators, which relies on height estimates due to Bombieri and Andr\'e.

papers.title: Fundamental solutions to Kolmogorov-Fokker-Planck equations with unbounded lower order terms
papers.abstract: We continue the study of fundamental solutions for equations involving Kolmogorov-Fokker-Planck operators with rough local or non-local diffusions. Here we consider possibly unbounded lower order terms, such as drifts and potentials. We prove existence and uniqueness of weak solutions and of an appropriate notion of fundamental solution for a wide class of kinetic equations. This is based on kinetic transfer of regularity and anisotropic embeddings.

papers.title: Uniformly Expanding Coupled Maps: Self-Consistent Transfer Operators and Propagation of Chaos
papers.abstract: We prove quantitative propagation of chaos in total variation, uniformly in time, for systems of $N$ deterministic uniformly expanding heterogeneously coupled maps. The local dynamics and interactions may vary between coordinates, so exchangeability is not required. Under assumptions (independent of the dimension) on expansion, regularity, and weak-coupling, we construct self-consistent transfer operators whose product evolutions approximate every fixed finite marginal. For a class of weakly dependent initial laws (containing products), the error is $O(N^{-1})$ on fixed time intervals and $O(\log N/N)$ uniformly in time. The finite-time rate is optimal within this class. An explicit family exhibits error of order $\sqrt{\log N}/N$ at times of order $\log N$, proving that a uniform $O(N^{-1})$ bound is impossible in general; the optimal correction remains open. The proof is based on ergodic theory: expansion preserves classes of regular, weakly dependent densities, while transfer-operator contraction controls error accumulation. These classes yield concentration estimates and allow direct comparison of densities, giving strong propagation of chaos without external noise. Under additional assumptions, we also obtain Gaussian approximation for empirical observables on fixed time intervals and invariant neighbourhoods of stable fixed points of the self-consistent operator.

papers.title: Fourier transform of nonlinear images of self-similar measures: quantitative aspects
papers.abstract: This paper relates to the Fourier decay properties of images of self-similar measures $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^k$ under nonlinear smooth maps $f \colon \mathbb{R}^k \to \mathbb{R}$. For example, we prove that if the linear parts of the similarities defining $\mu$ commute and the graph of $f$ has non-vanishing Gaussian curvature and $\kappa_2 > k/2$, then the Fourier dimension of the image measure is at least $\frac{2(2\kappa_2 - k)}{4 + 2\kappa_* - k}$, where $\kappa_2$ is the lower correlation dimension of $\mu$ and $\kappa_*$ is the Assouad dimension of the support of $\mu$. Under some additional assumptions on $\mu$, we use recent breakthroughs in the fractal uncertainty principle to obtain further improvements for the decay exponents. We give several applications to nonlinear arithmetic of self-similar sets $F$ in the line. For example, we prove that if $\dim_{\mathrm H} F > (\sqrt{65} - 5)/4 = 0.765\dots$ then the arithmetic product set $F \cdot F = \{ xy : x,y \in F \}$ has positive Lebesgue measure, while if $\dim_{\mathrm H} F > (-3 + \sqrt{41})/4 = 0.850\dots$ then $F \cdot F \cdot F$ has non-empty interior. One feature of the above results is that they do not require any separation conditions on the self-similar sets.

papers.title: Fourier inequalities and sign uncertainty
papers.abstract: Motivated by inequalities in Fourier analysis, we present an improvement on the lower bound for the sign uncertainty principle of Bourgain, Clozel and Kahane in high dimensions. Additionally, our methods can be used to match the existing Torquato-Stillinger lower bounds for the Cohn-Elkies linear program for sphere packing.
